lots.what_it_is: Robbery Under Arms by 'Rolf Boldrewood' (Thomas Alexander Browne), London: Remington and Co., 1888, 3 vols, the first book edition, in original green cloth blocked in black with gilt spines. The vol II title page in the photos reads ROLF BOLDERWOOD (the known misspelling), THREE VOLUMES, VOL II, Remington, Henrietta Street, 1888.
lots.score_reason: A genuine 1888 Remington first edition of a major Australian classic in original cloth. Dealer asks for better copies run A$3,950 (rebound) to A$10,048, so even a worn copy should be well over A$500 at auction, but there is no sold record to confirm a figure.

lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 1: three volumes in green cloth blocked in black (floral spray, butterfly, ruled frame), gilt spine titles Robbery Under Arms with VOL. III and VOL. II labels and REMINGTON at the feet; the third volume (presumably vol I) lies with its spine away, so its number is not legible. Photos 2 and 3: the vol II title page reads ROBBERY UNDER ARMS, A Story of Life and Adventure in the Bush and in the Goldfields of Australia, BY ROLF BOLDERWOOD, THREE VOLUMES, VOL II, LONDON, REMINGTON AND CO PUBLISHERS, HENRIETTA STREET COVENT GARDEN, 1888, [All Rights Reserved], with a Remington advert for the Czartoryski memoirs opposite. Scattered foxing and toning on the title leaf.
lots.condition: Cloth still fairly bright with crisp black blocking; spine ends rubbed and frayed (the heads worst), corners lightly bumped, page edges toned and dusty, scattered foxing on the vol II title leaf. Hinges, sewing, endpapers, half-titles and the vol I and III title pages are not shown.
lots.question_for_armitage: Please confirm all three volumes are the 1888 Remington edition (vols I and III title pages dated 1888), whether the half-titles and publisher's adverts are present and any leaves are missing, and the state of the inner hinges and sewing (cracked joints, loose gatherings, recasing or repairs). Any bookplates or inscriptions?

lots.what_it_is: Ten books: C.E.W. Bean, Official History of Australia in the War of 1914-18, vols I to VI (Angus & Robertson maroon cloth, mixed printings); W.S. Kent Hughes, Modern Crusaders (Melville & Mullen, 1918 or 1919); Jeannie Gunn, The Little Black Princess, whose cover and title page match the 1905 Moring first edition state (imprint not photographed); A Book of Beauty in a red patterned jacket (compiler not legible); and Giordano and Norman, Tasmanian Literary Landmarks (Hobart, 1984), inscribed by Margaret Giordano.
lots.score_reason: Bean vols I to VI, an early Little Black Princess and Modern Crusaders each have real collector value (older mainland hammers: Bean about A$30 to 60 a volume, a 1905 Gunn A$280, a signed Modern Crusaders A$450), but no result is recent, the Gunn's printing is unproven, and Hobart pays much less for WWI history sets (A$40 to 110).

lots.guide_summary: A composite lot, so the guide is the sum of each main title's range of surviving same or close entries: Bean vols I to VI A$188 to 900 (low: Davidson 2020 SOLD A$375 for 12 vols pro rata; high: Treloar ASK A$1,800 for 12 vols pro rata; Grant's asks A$418 for these six volumes), Little Black Princess A$79 to 1,200 (third printing ASK to Kay Craddock's 1905 first ASK; a 1905 first SOLD for A$280 at Leski in 2022), Modern Crusaders A$300 to 450 (ex-library ASK to a signed copy SOLD in Oct 2024), Tasmanian Literary Landmarks A$16.50 to 20 (ASK), A Book of Beauty no evidence; total A$583 to 2,570. Mix: 7 SOLD, all 2016 to Oct 2024 at Melbourne and Sydney rooms; 0 UNSOLD; the rest dealer ASKING. Tasmania: Gowans has none of these titles; its WWI and official history sets made A$40 to 110. Leski and all 78 Davidson sales were checked for these titles. Armitage's own results could not be searched (WebSearch cap). Rates: open.er-api.com, updated 19 Oct 2026 00:02 UTC: GBP 1 = A$1.91397, USD 1 = A$1.43581, EUR 1 = A$1.61297, A$1 = 109.949 JPY. AbeBooks listings from Australian sellers are given in the seller's own A$ price (AbeBooks converts at 0.71544 USD per AUD).

So keep_max_hammer = 0 and flip_max_hammer = 0. For scale only (old results): Bean vols I to VI about A$190 to 360 at A$31 to 60 a volume, Gunn 1905 first A$280 hammer, Modern Crusaders A$450 hammer for a signed copy; Hobart sold comparable WWI history sets for A$40 to 110. Armitage premium 22% including GST; inbound freight $0 (pickup at 9 Goodman Crt, Invermay).

Gowans '3 Australian in the War sets' (A$45) checked and found to be penny coin sets, not books.
lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 1: six Bean volumes in maroon cloth with gilt spines reading VOL I and VOL II The Story of Anzac and VOL III The A.I.F. in France 1916, then (left to right) VOL VI and VOL V The A.I.F. in France 1918 and VOL IV 1917, Angus & Robertson at the feet. The fourth, brighter red volume appears to read VOL VI (the 1942 only edition) rather than vol IV; the labels are small, so check at viewing. Modern Crusaders in orange/tan cloth lettered With the Light Horse through Sinai and Palestine. The Little Black Princess in light green pictorial cloth lettered BY JEANNIE GUNN, matching the Kay Craddock 1905 first edition photos (spine foot THE DE LA MORE PRESS), whereas the September 1906 third printing (Renaissance Books photo) reads BY Mrs AENEAS GUNN. The lot's title page has the same setting as the 1905 first, but its imprint, the spine foot and the last leaf are not shown. A Book of Beauty in a chipped red patterned jacket, label subtitle illegible. Tasmanian Literary Landmarks title page inscribed 'To Mollie - best wishes, Margaret Giordano'.
lots.condition: Bean volumes: cloth bright with clear gilt, top edges dusty, interiors unseen. Modern Crusaders: cloth soiled and darkened, corners worn. Little Black Princess: cloth rubbed and soiled at the edges, spine and hinges unseen. A Book of Beauty: jacket chipped and torn at the edges. Tasmanian Literary Landmarks: clean paperback.
lots.question_for_armitage: For The Little Black Princess, please check the imprint at the foot of the title page (1905 or 1906) and its back, the spine foot (De La More Press or Melville and Mullen), whether the text ends with a colophon on p.108 (first printing) or with press opinions (later printing), and that the 24 plates and map are present and the hinges sound. For the Bean volumes, the edition dates on the title-page backs and any ex-library marks or foxing; for Modern Crusaders, the date on the title page and whether the folding map is present; and the compiler and publisher of A Book of Beauty.
